catalog_quote: In Bahnar phonological words are either monosyllabic or bisyllabic. Bisyllabic words consist of a stressed "main syllable" preceded by an unstressed "presyllable". Monosyllabic words consist of a (usually) stressed "main syllable". [p. vi] ... The presyllable vowel is ơ except after glottal stop where a occurs in pronounced speech but may change to ơ in normal speech ... There is no length contrast in the presyllable vowels. [p. x] ... Hyphen indicates juncture between phonological words that comprise a larger morphological word ... [p. xii]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Bahnar words are monosyllables or sesquisyllables (presyllable + main syllable). Stress falls on the main syllable, which is always the final syllable of the phonological word; the presyllable (C + schwa/a, no length contrast) is unstressed. Monosyllables are normally stressed.
new_statements.exceptions: Monosyllabic words are only 'usually' stressed (the hedge is not explained; presumably unstressed particles/clitics). Presyllable vowel is schwa, or a after glottal stop (pp. xi-xii).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word. Larger morphological words (reduplicative series, compounds) are written with hyphens marking 'juncture between phonological words that comprise a larger morphological word', i.e. each phonological word keeps its own stressed main syllable. Dictionary citation forms; no phrase-level prosody discussed. Dourisboure 1889 (Kontum dialect) adds only that Bahnar has no tones, just long and short vowels.
new_statements.identity_note: The 1979 SIL dictionary whose phonology preface carries the statement is explicitly based on the Plei Bong-Mang Yang dialect (Gia Lai province), with additional entries from the Golar dialect (east of Pleiku) and the Kontum dialect; the statement is made for 'Bahnar' generally. No separate Glottolog dialect code assigned here. Note Glottolog 5.x now files bahn1262 under West Bahnaric > Tampuon-Bahnar, while the dictionary itself discusses North/South/Central Bahnaric affiliation.
